idioms.meaning_en: Quran has more complex connotations. The speaker in 90.6 is an affluent but niggardly person, and he makes the remark upon being asked to spend for the sake of the poor and the needy. thus suggests, first, that it is in all probability a small amount of wealth he spends, but that he thinks it is a large amount; and, second, that, deep down in his heart, he thinks that the wealth he has given away he might have given away in vain. Further, Page 397 of 404 the use of the word is ironical: from the viewpoint of the Day of Judgment, the wealth he has spent is in fact wasted. He says, “I have spent/given away so much wealth” To perform an arduous task [ = a good deed]

idioms.meaning_en: Compare the construction in 69:3 (referred to as i) and 33:63 (referred to as ii): i and ii are usually considered interchangeable, but the Quranic usage suggests that there is some difference between the two. First, i indicates the momentous or prodigious nature of something, but that is not necessarily the case with ii. Second, i implies that the listener either lacks all knowledge about the thing in question or is unaware of its true significance, whereas ii implies that the listener may have formed some idea of what is being talked about, but could be grossly mistaken in his estimation.
